subject: Control/Data Plane Demarcation and HA tether for private VPC deployment
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-example.com, networks@cloudx-partner.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Control/Data Plane Demarcation and HA tether for private VPC deployment

Hi team —

Thanks for the sync yesterday. Per follow-up with Acme and CloudX, I'm sending the first-pass doc and two diagrams (attached) that show how Redwood's control plane will sit in the customer-managed VPC while the data plane lives on the on-prem GPU cluster. Key asks below.

Summary (high level):
- Control plane: managed by Redwood but runs in a private VPC peered (transit) to Acme's networking hub. Control-plane endpoints are restricted to management subnets and our egress is via a customer-controlled NAT/proxy.
- Data plane: on-prem inference nodes with a direct eBGP/overlay path to the control plane for metrics, heartbeats, and model artifact pulls. Data plane only accepts proxied requests from the control plane; customer traffic never transits Redwood-hosted public endpoints.
- HA tether: we propose a dual-path keepalive — primary over the private transit and secondary via an encrypted fallback link to CloudX for cross-region failover.

Immediate asks:
1) Acme: confirm the proposed demarcation boundary (diagram A) is acceptable for your security team. Specifically we need approval for outbound TLS to our control-plane FQDNs from the management subnets.
2) CloudX: can you confirm the recommended overlay (WireGuard/MPLS) options for the secondary tether and whether you can support a BGP session for prefix announcement in failover?
3) Infra (Aditya + Soojin): please review the attached config-snippets.txt. I put recommended firewall rules and the process for bootstrapping the KV cache on first model pull.

Attachments:
- redwood-private-vpc-demarcation-v1.pdf (reference diagrams and sequence flows)
- ha-tether-diagram.drawio (failover path + BGP notes)
- config-snippets.txt (example iptables, WireGuard, and systemd unit snippets)

Timing: Acme needs an architecture approval by end of week to keep the Nov deploy window. If we can't confirm, recommended fallback is a temporary transit appliance in Acme's cloud account.

Thanks — please reply inline.

— Ava Chen
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control/Data Plane Demarcation and HA tether for private VPC deployment

Thanks, Ava — reviewed the artifacts. Quick notes:

1) Control plane endpoints
- We should publish a short-lived client cert rotation plan in addition to TLS; customer NAT/proxy should allow outgoing 443 and 8443 to our endpoints. The reason: some customers run deep packet inspection that breaks TLS SNI for long-lived sessions.

2) Data plane bootstrap
- Recommend model artifacts be pulled over HTTPS from an S3-compatible gateway inside Acme's network (saves cross-tenant egress). We'll sign artifacts with our key. See config-snippets.txt lines ~40-72 for the sha256 checks.

3) HA tether details
- Primary keepalive: persistent TLS + gRPC heartbeat on port 12000.
- Secondary: encrypted WireGuard with BGP only for prefix announcement for limited failover; prefix size will be /32 for the control-plane endpoint to avoid broad route leak.

4) Firewall rules (summary)
- Allow outbound 12000 (TCP) to control-plane FQDNs from data-plane nodes.
- Allow inbound management from management subnets to data-plane on port 22 (jump box) only.

Open question for CloudX: can you support BGP MD5 and AS_PATH filtering? If yes we'll lock down the failover plan.

Appended a short inline diff from the diagram — see page 3 of the PDF for recommended NAT exemption.

— Aditya
Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Control/Data Plane Demarcation and HA tether for private VPC deployment

Ava / Aditya — thanks for the detailed diagrams. Security flagged two items that need clarification before we can sign off:

1) Data exfil risk: security asked whether model artifacts or inference logs will be buffered temporarily on the data plane and what retention policy applies.
2) Fallback path ops: the failover path to CloudX is okay, but we need an ops playbook showing detection thresholds and automatic vs manual failover. Also need an SLA for the secondary link.

Quick answers to your asks:
- We can allow outbound 443/8443 from management subnets but require mutual TLS (mTLS) to our proxy for egress termination.
- We can support a WireGuard overlay managed through CloudX but they cannot run arbitrary BGP announcements from our account; any BGP must be co-ordinated through our network team (they will open a ticket if needed).

Can you supply the retention table and the proposed ops playbook by Tue EOD? Without that, security won't clear production traffic.

— Jordan Lee
Lead Ops Engineer, Acme Logistics
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-example.com, ava_chen@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, networks@cloudx-partner.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control/Data Plane Demarcation and HA tether for private VPC deployment

Jordan — appreciate the security review. Drafting the retention and playbook now. High-level answers here to unblock the conversation:

Retention and telemetry:
- Inference logs: stored locally for 72 hours on data-plane nodes with automatic rotation; only aggregated telemetry (metrics, health) forwarded to control plane. No raw prompt/response payloads are retained beyond 72 hours unless customer elects extended logging (opt-in).
- Model artifacts: pulled on demand and kept in a read-only artifact cache; cache eviction policy is LRU with an admin-configurable TTL (default 7 days). Artifacts are signed and checksummed.

Failover/playbook (short):
- Detection: persistent gRPC heartbeat missed on 3 consecutive 10s intervals => flag degraded.
- Automated action: attempt restart and re-establish WireGuard; if still degraded after 3x restarts, escalate to on-call and begin controlled traffic drain to local fallback appliance.
- Manual failover: network team can trigger BGP announcement via CloudX via runbook link (I will add the CloudX contact).
- SLA: Redwood will commit to a best-effort secondary link; exact SLA is between Acme and CloudX (we will operate the control-plane failover logic).

Attaching a short one-page playbook and retention table; will push the full Ops runbook to the Drive link today.

— Soojin
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: playbook-v1.pdf, retention-table.csv (attached to this message)
From: networks@cloudx-partner.com <networks@cloudx-partner.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acme-example.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control/Data Plane Demarcation and HA tether for private VPC deployment

Hi all — CloudX network ops here. We can support the WireGuard overlay and a BGP session for limited prefix failover. A few operational notes:

- BGP MD5 is supported; we'll enforce strict AS_PATH filters and only accept the /32 control-plane prefix from Redwood's session.
- We require a peering config ticket at least 48 hrs before any automated announcement; manual runbook initiation is preferred for initial testing.
- We recommend using our managed NAT gateway for artifact pulls (saves on NAT gateway footprint in Acme's edge).

We'll link the ticket template in the Drive doc and will stand up a test peer for the week of Nov 15 for your test harness.

— CloudX Network Ops
(end of thread)
